classification.difficultyReason: Apply the bearing convention at the supplied north arrow, measuring towards each point and converting the northwest direction to a reflex clockwise angle.

content.prompt: Using a protractor, measure the bearing of:

spec.description: A and B are horizontally level, northwest and northeast of C respectively. Their relative offsets reproduce the source raster without adding connecting segments. A vertical north arrow rises from C. Ordinary source blue strokes and red point markers use house black.
spec.mathematics: Relative source offsets from C are A=(-205,94) and B=(261,94), up to uniform scale. These give measured bearings approximately 295 degrees and 070 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied points, labels and north arrow are visible; no connecting segments, measured angles or answers are supplied.

answer.worked:
Place the protractor at $C$. The smaller angle from north towards $A$ is approximately $65^{\circ}$ anticlockwise.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }C&=360^{\circ}-65^{\circ}\\\text{Bearing of }A\text{ from }C&=295^{\circ}\mathrm{T}\end{align*}$$
Place the protractor at $C$ and measure clockwise from north towards $B$. The angle is approximately $70^{\circ}$, so the three-digit true bearing is $070^{\circ}\mathrm{T}$.
